correctness.rationale: Finite-field and projective definitions are explicit; a nonscalar element fixes a proper vertex only on one of q²+1 quadratic-subfield lines, with stabilizer H of order q+1. Point and hyperplane stabilizers are trivial. Counting the three flag-edge types and complete flags yields orbit-cell counts and χ=q³−q²+1. Solomon–Tits gives simple connectivity of the original complex; Armstrong gives π1=G/H cyclic of order q²+1; cellular dimension two and H1 finite force H2 free of rank q²(q−1). The q=2 and q=3 integral orbit-boundary computations and Smith reductions independently agree. No full homotopy equivalence is asserted.

value.rationale: The finite-field A3 building and its full Singer automorphism are intrinsic objects. The theorem supplies their complete fundamental-group and integral-homology classification for every finite field, including even and odd characteristic, and reveals unbounded cyclic torsion created by a nonfree quotient of a simply connected building. This is a natural integral invariant family not supplied by the published flat-orbit counts or the prior single binary case.
